prompt.context: Your client is a real estate developer, Lizette's Luxury Properties, and is currently assessing a new project idea in Costa Rica. Costa Rica has a beautiful coastline which has historically been difficult to access. The nearest airport was over six hours away. As of last year, a new airport was constructed only a half hour away. There has been an investment boom in the region due to the increasing number of tourists (popular with Americans and Asians). The Mandarin Oriental and The Four Seasons, two prominent luxury hotel chains, were the first to enter this market with a 250-room hotel each.
prompt.question: Should your client invest in the tourism opportunity created by the new airport? Would you recommend that s/he enter the market?

clarifying_info.q: What has the client built in the past?
clarifying_info.a: The client has focused on hi-rise apartments (50%) and luxury condominiums (50%) but wants to enter the hotel arena. They have focused on world-class beaches such as Playa del Carmen, Marbella, Coral Beach, Tahiti, Fiji, Maldives, and Mikonos.

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of the tourist market?
clarifying_info.a: 875,000 tourists per year (assume 350 operating days in a calendar year). Average duration of stay is 4 nights. Average hotel check is $2,000.

clarifying_info.q: Who else is considering entering the market?
clarifying_info.a: Other hotel chains thinking of entering include Starwood, Peninsula, and Imperial Hotels.

The client has short-listed three lots: Lover's Lair ($2MM land, $30K/room construction cost, $250 operating cost/night, 500 rooms, $450 price/night); Paradise Lost ($4MM land, $28K/room, $200 operating cost/night, 1000 rooms, $400 price/night); Fookwah Heights ($6MM land, $25K/room, $150 operating cost/night, 1500 rooms, $350 price/night).
At 10% ROI the company target is to recover investments within one year. Average occupancy is 50%. There are 350 operating days per year. Operating expenses are 100% variable.

exhibits.title: Three Available Lots — Cost and Revenue Summary
exhibits.shows: A table comparing three hotel lot options across land cost, construction cost per room, operating cost per room per night, room capacity, and price per night

framework: Core Competencies: assess client's relevant skills and gaps for hotel development
Market Attractiveness / Five Forces: market size, competition, supplier power, substitutes, barriers to entry, buyer power
ROI Analysis: compare return on investment across the three available lots
Project Feasibility / Success Factors: identify key operational and strategic concerns before committing

questions.prompt: What is the total market size in tourist nights and implied room rate per night?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates calculate total tourist nights and derive an implied rate to contextualize the market. 875,000 tourists × 4 nights = 3.5 million tourist nights. 3.5M nights / 350 days = 10,000 tourists per night. $2,000 average check / 4 nights = $500 per night implied market rate.

math.setup: Total tourist nights = 875,000 tourists × 4 nights/tourist. Tourists per night = total nights / 350 days. Implied rate = $2,000 / 4 nights.

questions.prompt: Calculate the ROI for each of the three lots and recommend one to maximize return on investment.
questions.guidance: Candidates should apply the formula ROI = (Operating Profit − Initial Investment) / Initial Investment, using 50% occupancy and 350 nights/year. Fookwah Heights yields the highest ROI at ~20.7% and exceeds the 10% target. Paradise Lost is close to target at 9.4%. Lover's Lair falls well short at 2.9%.

math.setup: Revenue = Price/night × Rooms × 350 nights × 50% occupancy. Operating Cost = OpEx/night × Rooms × 350 × 50%. Operating Profit = Revenue − Operating Cost. Initial Investment = Cost/room × Rooms + Land Cost. ROI = (Operating Profit − Initial Investment) / Initial Investment.
steps: Lover's Lair: Operating Profit = ($450−$250)×500×350×0.5 = $17.5M; Investment = $30K×500+$2M = $17M; Net = $0.5M; ROI = 0.5/17 = 2.9%
Paradise Lost: Operating Profit = ($400−$200)×1000×350×0.5 = $35M; Investment = $28K×1000+$4M = $32M; Net = $3M; ROI = 3/32 = 9.4%
Fookwah Heights: Operating Profit = ($350−$150)×1500×350×0.5 = $52.5M; Investment = $25K×1500+$6M = $43.5M; Net = $9M; ROI = 9/43.5 = 20.7%
math.answer: Fookwah Heights has the highest ROI at 20.7%, well above the 10% target. Paradise Lost is near the hurdle at 9.4%. Lover's Lair is the weakest at 2.9%.

questions.prompt: What factors should be considered in determining the overall feasibility of the project?
questions.guidance: Good answers cover competition strategy (low cost vs. high service vs. packages), financing options (potential government incentives/tax breaks given job creation), and how competitors are positioned to avoid market flooding. Excellent answers also address: how client can leverage existing construction and beachfront development expertise; whether to manage the hotel directly or partner with an established operator (e.g., Starwood, Hilton); how to address barriers to entry (government permits, sewage, water, beachfront access) and potentially use them defensively.

brainstorming.prompt: List the key factors to be considered in determining the feasibility of the project.

categories.name: Competitive Strategy
ideas: Where to compete: low cost, high service, best-in-class, packages
How to differentiate from Mandarin Oriental and Four Seasons already in market
Risk of market flooding if Starwood, Peninsula, and Imperial all enter

categories.name: Client Capabilities & Structure
ideas: Leverage construction expertise and beachfront property judgment
No direct hotel management experience — consider operating partner (Starwood, Hilton)

categories.name: Financing
ideas: High capital requirement is a barrier and a constraint
Government incentives possible (jobs created): tax deductions, free utilities
Debt vs. equity structure for construction

categories.name: Regulatory & Operational
ideas: Government permits and approvals for construction
Access to sewage and water infrastructure
Beachfront property rights and environmental regulations

categories.name: Market Risk
ideas: Dependence on government tourism advertising spend
Reliance on travel agents and e-vendors (consolidated buyer power)
Competition from substitute destinations: Disneyland, Vegas, Bermuda, other 'paradise' locales

recommendation: Recommend entering the market, specifically by developing Fookwah Heights, which delivers a 20.7% ROI against the 10% hurdle rate
The market is large (10,000 tourists per night at $500/night implied rate) and the client has proven construction expertise at world-class beach destinations
risks: Hotel management is a new capability — operational risk without a hospitality partner
Market could become crowded if all prospective entrants (Starwood, Peninsula, Imperial) follow through
Buyer power is high due to travel agency consolidation and e-vendor proliferation
Dependence on continued government investment in airport and tourism promotion
next_steps: Evaluate an operating partnership with an established hotel chain to bridge the management capability gap
Secure government permits and assess infrastructure (sewage, water) before committing capital
Model sensitivity of ROI to occupancy rates below 50% and assess downside scenarios
Investigate financing options including potential government incentives tied to job creation
